review_notes: I read the whole file: the preamble, the single `solution` theorem statement and its proof. The preamble has `attribute [-instance]` and `attribute [-simp]` lines. These look like generated boilerplate that switches off imported instances and simp lemmas locally. The file declares no definitions, no `@[simp]` lemmas, and no `simp` or `simp only` calls. The proof uses only `intro`, `obtain`, `funext`, `rw`, `norm_num` and `exact`, with explicit imported theorems. So there is no simp interface here to criticise: no missing canonical simp lemma, no orientation problem, no competing rules, no expansion, and no cycle. I did not open the imported files to check whether the simp lemmas that are disabled are well-designed. A problem with those lemmas would belong to the files that declare them, not to this one. I found nothing justified under this rubric.
